questions.question: Explain how 1976 affected exile and the armed struggle.
questions.expected_answer: Thousands (several thousand to over ten thousand) left via Botswana, Swaziland, Lesotho to Tanzania, Zambia, Angola. Most joined ANC (Tambo's established exile structures, camps, support); some PAC, some BC. MK revived: training in Angola, USSR, East Germany; Sasol attack June 1980, Koeberg 1982, Church Street bomb May 1983 (19 killed incl. civilians); debate; TRC found violations by both sides, state's far greater. SOMAFCO, Mazimbu, Tanzania, 1978; Solomon Mahlangu, Goch Street, hanged 6 April 1979.

questions.question: Explain how repression increased after 1976.
questions.expected_answer: Detention without trial, torture, deaths in custody. Steve Biko: banned 1973; arrested 18 August 1977; assaulted in Port Elizabeth; driven more than 1 000 km to Pretoria; died 12 September 1977 aged 30; Kruger "left me cold"; hunger-strike claim; Woods and Zille exposed; inquest blamed no one; funeral about 15 000; TRC refused amnesty to officers. Black Wednesday 19 October 1977: nineteen organisations banned (SASO, BPC, SASM, SSRC, Christian Institute), The World and Weekend World banned, Qoboza detained, Woods and Naudé banned.

questions.question: Explain the international responses, reforms and new resistance after 1976.
questions.expected_answer: International: UN Resolution 418 (4 November 1977) mandatory arms embargo; Armscor expanded; Gleneagles Agreement 1977; Sullivan Principles 1977; anti-apartheid campaigns. Reforms: Vorster resigned 1978 (Information Scandal), P.W. Botha "adapt or die"; Wiehahn: black unions recognised 1979; Riekert; Department of Education and Training 1979; community councils, Black Local Authorities 1982; reform and repression. New resistance: AZAPO 1978, COSAS 1979, 1980 boycotts, unions, civics, UDF 1983; leaders like Murphy Morobe; Mashinini died in exile 1990; "liberation before education" debate; NECC 1986. Memory: Youth Day, Hector Pieterson Museum 2002.
